resources.name: shairport-sync
resources.note: C implementation of an AirPlay 1 and AirPlay 2 audio receiver; reference for RAOP packet format. Actively maintained, tested against current iOS.

resources.name: UxPlay
resources.note: AirPlay 2 mirroring + audio receiver; documents the AirPlay 2 RTSP/mirror/audio pipeline. GPL-3.0.

resources.name: AIRPLAY_PROTOCOL.md (centuryplay2)
resources.note: Comprehensive AirPlay 1 (RAOP) protocol reference doc built from RE and implementation experience: RTSP control, session establishment, audio streaming, time sync, encryption.

resources.name: Reverse-engineering history writeup
resources.note: Contemporary report on Laird's key extraction from the AirPort Express ROM and the original ShairPort emulator.

entries.reverse_engineered: Developer James Laird extracted Apple's private AirPlay keys from an AirPort Express ROM chip and published the ShairPort emulator, proving third-party devices could receive AirPlay streams. The community has since documented the RAOP RTSP session flow, RSA/AES-128-CBC key exchange, RTP audio packet format, mDNS (_raop._tcp) discovery, and the AirPlay 2 pair-setup/pair-verify + FairPlay handshake framing.
entries.still_unknown: Parts of the AirPlay 2 video mirroring encryption and newer HomeKit-tied pairing flows are only partially documented; some FairPlay handshake details remain closed.
entries.what_it_does: Wireless audio/video/photo streaming from iOS/macOS/iTunes to receivers (AirPort Express, Apple TV, speakers). AirPlay 1 uses RTSP control over TCP port 5000 with RTP audio over UDP; AirPlay 2 adds multi-room sync, an event port, and a FairPlay-protected pairing handshake.

resources.name: freedelity/apple-lightning
resources.note: Arduino programs to sniff the Lightning ACC_ID pin and serial bus, spoof a genuine Lightning controller identity, and MITM an authenticated MFi accessory session.

resources.name: Hackaday Lightning connector RE
resources.note: Ramtin Amin's teardown: Tristar (CBTL1608A1) identified as the accessory/debug/baseband/JTAG mux, desoldered onto a breakout board and driven from an STM32 Discovery board.

resources.name: Dynamic pin assignment analysis
resources.note: Peter Bradstock's (Double Helix Cables) continuity measurements proving top/bottom pin pairing and orientation-dependent pin assignment.

entries.reverse_engineered: Community RE established: dynamic pin assignment (symmetric power pins, asymmetric data pins), the ACC_ID identification pin protocol, the accessory UART serial bus, and the Tristar/CBTL1608A1 mux chip that switches accessory UART / debug UART / baseband / SoC / JTAG. Arduino-based tools can sniff the ACC_ID pin, sniff/spoof accessory identity, and man-in-the-middle the accessory serial bus after MFi authentication completes.
entries.still_unknown: The full MFi authentication chip cryptography; complete accessory-class command set beyond serial/UART accessories.
entries.what_it_does: 8-pin reversible digital connector (iPhone 5 through iPhone 14) carrying USB, UART accessory serial, and audio. Pins are dynamically assigned per insertion orientation; accessories carry an authentication chip and identify via the ACC_ID pin.

entries.protocol: Sonos local control (UPnP/SOAP + local Control API)

resources.name: SoCo/SoCo
resources.note: The canonical open-source Python library for Sonos control: discovery, transport, queue, groups, favorites, alarms, events. No cloud, no Sonos account required.

resources.name: x2rock
resources.note: Rust CLI + MPRIS2 server covering both transports: raw UPnP/SOAP probing and the undocumented local Control API over WebSocket.

resources.name: sonosify
resources.note: Async Python API over UPnP with live event subscriptions (AVTransport/RenderingControl events).

resources.name: sonos-cli
resources.note: Bun/TypeScript port of SoCo logic; documents SOAP envelope construction and the local API client.

entries.reverse_engineered: The UPnP service surface was mapped from the speakers' own SCPD descriptors: 16 UPnP services, SSDP discovery, GENA event subscriptions for live state. The local WebSocket/HTTPS Control API (port 1443, X-Sonos-Api-Key header, mDNS _sonos._tcp.local discovery) was reverse engineered from speaker firmware and app traffic, enabling cloud-free local control including grouping and per-room volume.
entries.still_unknown: Sonos can change or close the undocumented local API in firmware updates; SMAPI music-service auth flows are only partially mapped.
entries.what_it_does: LAN control of Sonos speakers: transport, volume, EQ, grouping, queue, favorites, alarms. Historically UPnP/SOAP on port 1400 (AVTransport, RenderingControl, ZoneGroupTopology, ContentDirectory, DeviceProperties); newer firmware also exposes an undocumented local Control API over HTTPS on port 1443 with JSON bodies.

entries.protocol: DJI DroneID / DUML / OcuSync link analysis

resources.name: DroneSecurity (RUB-SysSec)
resources.note: SDR-based DJI DroneID receiver from the NDSS'23 paper 'Drone Security and the Mysterious Case of DJI's DroneID'; works live or on captures.

resources.name: DUMLmap
resources.note: Passive DUML protocol knowledge: OcuSync 3 binding handshakes, UNR0 partition format, IMAH 2018 firmware container format (signed+encrypted, keys documented).

resources.name: dji-drone-hijacking (arXiv 2309.05913)
resources.note: Proof-of-concept command replay/injection against the DJI Enhanced Wi-Fi (Mini SE) protocol variant, per the 'Behind The Wings' paper.

resources.name: OcuSync O3/O4 signal analysis
resources.note: Community signal analysis of OcuSync generations: FHSS parameters, hopping rates, dual-band behavior.

entries.reverse_engineered: Ruhr University Bochum / CISPA researchers (NDSS'23) reverse engineered the DroneID broadcast and built an SDR receiver decoding drone and operator positions from OcuSync 2.0 frames (BladeRF/USRP, tested on Mini 2 / Mavic Air 2). Separately, DUML command structures were mapped from firmware RE (Ghidra on dji_wlm / dji_network binaries, OcuSync 3 binding handshakes captured at 5825 MHz), and an academic team demonstrated command-stream replay/injection against the DJI Enhanced Wi-Fi protocol variant (arXiv 2309.05913).
entries.still_unknown: Full OcuSync control-link encryption keys and the complete proprietary command set; newer O4 implementations only partially analyzed.
entries.what_it_does: DroneID is DJI's Remote-ID-style broadcast (drone + operator position) sent over the OcuSync link; DUML is the internal command protocol between DJI flight controller components and the mobile app/RC.

resources.name: joshwardell/model3dbc
resources.note: Community reverse-engineered Model 3/Y CAN DBC (Model3CAN.dbc, ~159 messages, MIT). The primary source other projects vendor.

resources.name: commaai/opendbc
resources.note: openpilot's DBC collection including Tesla; used as cross-check reference for signal usage and checksum/counter enforcement.

resources.name: awesome-automotive-can-id
resources.note: Curated index of CAN ID resources across brands, including Tesla Model 3/S/X spreadsheets and DBCs.

entries.reverse_engineered: The community decoded 150+ Model 3/Y CAN messages into DBC files: pack voltage/current (BMS_hvBusStatus), drive inverter speed/status (DI_speed, DI_systemStatus) including additive checksums, EPAS steering control (GTW_epasControl, DAS_steeringControl), and body/chassis signals. Cross-checked against comma.ai's openpilot Tesla integration, which consumes these signals for driver assistance.
entries.still_unknown: Exact production message cadences, some safety-relevant checksums, and HW4/newer platform message layouts.
entries.what_it_does: Internal vehicle networks (Vehicle CAN, Chassis CAN) carrying battery, drivetrain, steering (EPAS), and autopilot signals. Tesla publishes no DBC or signal documentation.

resources.name: Zigbee2MQTT
resources.note: Open bridge replacing vendor hubs (Hue, IKEA, Xiaomi): pairs Hue bulbs directly via Touchlink, controls brightness/color/effects over MQTT. Loses Hue Entertainment/Sync, which stay proprietary.

resources.name: Hue firmware URL RE thread
resources.note: Community reverse engineering of Philips' unpublished per-device OTA firmware URLs, catalogued for the zigbee-OTA firmware index.

resources.name: Moving Hue to Zigbee2MQTT (video guide)
resources.note: Walkthrough of three factory-reset methods (app deletion, Touchlink with serial, Hue Dimmer) to migrate bulbs off the Hue Bridge.

entries.reverse_engineered: The community showed Hue bulbs pair directly to any open Zigbee coordinator: Touchlink commissioning (even via the bulb's printed serial number, no bridge needed), standard Zigbee clusters for brightness/color/color-temperature/effects, and reverse-engineered Hue firmware OTA URLs (firmware-hue storage endpoints, per-device unique URLs catalogued in the zigbee-OTA index). Zigbee2MQTT fully replaces the Hue Bridge, exposing every bulb as an MQTT device; powered Hue bulbs act as mesh routers.
entries.still_unknown: Hue Entertainment low-latency streaming protocol and Hue Sync remain proprietary and bridge-dependent.
entries.what_it_does: Smart lighting control. Hue bulbs speak standard Zigbee (Light Link, now Zigbee 3.0) but were historically locked to the proprietary Hue Bridge; OTA firmware URLs were unpublished.

resources.name: HAP-python
resources.note: Python implementation of the HomeKit Accessory Protocol: build your own accessories pairable from the iOS Home app, camera support, Home Assistant integration.

resources.name: magrgb-controller (HAP-BLE RE)
resources.note: Documents HAP-BLE pairing (SRP, pair-setup characteristic 0x4C) and characteristic control against a commercial HAP-BLE device, including advertisement quirks.

entries.reverse_engineered: HAP was reimplemented from scratch in Python (HAP-python): accessory definitions, QR-code pairing, asyncio event loop, camera accessory support, and Home Assistant integration. HAP-over-BLE was further documented by community projects driving nonstandard advertisements through pairing state machines (e.g., Secretlab/Nanoleaf MAGRGB strip: dual HAP-BLE + vendor BLE advertisements, SRP pair-setup flow, HSV characteristic control).
entries.still_unknown: Newer HAP features tied to Apple silicon secure elements and some vendor-proprietary characteristic extensions.
entries.what_it_does: Pairing and control protocol for HomeKit accessories (HAP over IP and HAP over BLE): SRP-based pairing with setup codes, ChaCha20-Poly1305 encrypted sessions, accessory/service/characteristic model (e.g., Lightbulb service with Hue/Saturation/Brightness characteristics).

evidence_labels.confirmed: Working open implementation exists and is actively used.
evidence_labels.likely: Partial RE documented with tools, but no complete open stack.

methodology: Entries document community reverse engineering of proprietary protocols: what was figured out, working open implementations, and what remains unknown. Evidence labels: 'confirmed' = a working open implementation exists and is in active use; 'likely' = partial RE documented with tools, but no complete open stack. All resource URLs were verified live via web search on 2026-10-07. Nothing here is invented.
